subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I’m sure that time / changes things, but it / didn’t change anything / unlike my perception of you.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"unlike my perception of you"** is incorrect because "unlike" is used to compare two things directly, but in this context, it creates an awkward and unclear contrast. It doesn't properly convey the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
• The intended meaning of the sentence is that time changes many things, but it did not change anything except the speaker's perception of the person being addressed.
 
• To convey this contrast correctly, we should use** "except" instead of "unlike".**
 
• Thus, the error is located in **Option 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I’m sure that time **changes things, but it* *didn’t change anything ****except ****my perception of you."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "didn’t change anything" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• 2: "changes things, but it" – This segment is grammatically correct. It presents a general truth about time.
 
• **3: "I’m sure that time"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
